chunks: From him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sam'ah and 'Ali ibn Khalid, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Amr al-Kha'shami, from 'Amr ibn al-Bara', who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Our companions say that if a man divorces his wife once or a hundred times, it is only one divorce. And it had reached us from you and from your fathers that they said: if he divorces [her] once or a hundred times, it is only one.' He said: 'It is as it reached you.'
ai.seo_question: Does multiple divorce pronouncements in one session count as one or three divorces in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia position on *talqah wahidah* (single divorce), confirming that multiple pronouncements in one session constitute only one revocable divorce, contrary to the Sunni view of immediate irrevocability. Imam al-Sadiq’s affirmation validates the established practice of the companions, highlighting the jurisprudential consensus (*ijma'*) within the school regarding the counting of divorces. This ruling carries significant practical implications for marital stability, allowing the couple a period of reconciliation before the finality of divorce.
